I do understand that the confederate flag has become a symbol for many white supremacists. However, by denying that the confederate flag is part of US history, it stigmatizes history in a way that promotes further revisionism of the past. A lot history books fail to reflect the economic realities of slavery in the southern states.

Now, I am in no way a slavery apologist, but recognize that cotton trade was one of the major reasons that slavery was still being used int he south. Many people in the south believed that when technology advanced to the state where they no longer required slaves, slavery would dissipate naturally. However, this was foolish for southern slaveowners to assume.

Also, the confederate flag was not just a symbol for those who were against emancipation. It was a symbol for those who did not believe in one, single unified government, similar ideas that are now represented in libertarianism and modern day conservatism.

Now, I am basically going off of what I learned in my university classes, and not necessarily reading any sources to back up my information. So if I got any historical facts wrong, or have anything to add, feel free to correct me.

tl;dr the confederate flag has historical meaning that is not necessarily in line with what modern day "confederates" are using it to represent today, and thus I believe that it should not be taken off of shelves. I believe that the act of doing so will promote further rewriting of history.
